chunks: From him, from his father, from one of our companions who said:

Pigeons were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him, 'It has reached me that Umar saw a pigeon flying and a man running under it, so Umar said, 'A satan running under a satan.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'What was Ismail among you?' So it was said, 'A truthful one.' So he said, 'The remaining pigeons of the Sanctuary are from a pigeon of Ismail.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the pigeons of the Haram in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the popular notion that the pigeons of the Haram are 'shaitan' by linking them to Prophet Ismail (AS), known as 'al-Siddiq', thereby establishing a sacred lineage for the birds. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual purity of the Haram's natural inhabitants, contrasting with the broader Islamic tradition that often views them as neutral or symbolic of jinn. The hadith serves to elevate the status of the pigeons from mere creatures to blessed entities associated with a major prophet.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from one of our companions who said,

‘The pigeons were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It has reached me that Umar saw a pigeon flying by and a man was running under it, so Umar said, ‘A satan<sup>la</sup> underneath a satan<sup>la</sup>’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What was Ismail<sup>as</sup> among you all?’ So it was said, ‘A truthful one’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The remaining pigeons of the Sanctuary are from a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 18. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “

Once, pigeons were mentioned before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and a man said, ‘It has come to my knowledge that once ‘Umar saw a pigeon flying and a man underneath was running. ‘Umar then said, “One Satan runs under another Satan.” Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘(It is because) Tsma‘il was not there with you.’ Someone then asked, ‘Was he (Tsma‘il) a friend (of pigeons)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The pigeons of al-Haram (the sacred area) are of the remaining pigeons of Tsma‘il.’”
